findings.claim: The extracted Drive tree contains a generated v7 concept corpus index with 655 documents, 3762 inter-document relations and 14690477 text characters across eight categories; 561 documents are <=30 days old, 28 are 31-90 days old and 66 are 91-240 days old.
findings.implication: Use the existing index/version/correlation layer as the high-throughput semantic manifest backbone instead of rereading the 663552000-byte tarball serially. Preserve its scope boundary: it is a concept/text submanifest, not automatically the entire Drive denominator.

findings.claim: KORRELATIONEN.md records 2922 lexical-similarity relations, 681 explicit mentions and 159 version-follow relations, including long repeated version chains for benchmark, architecture, memory and evaluation documents.
findings.implication: Level-0 ingestion must collapse version ancestry and supersession before counting independent evidence; same-name documents are often versions, not replications.

findings.claim: The prior interpretation that NMK/meta-vocabulary emerged in round 3 is contradicted by a direct recount against schwarm.db: xeno1 already contains the seed in round 1 (2/67 document contributions; 4/67 raw responses), then 52/66 and 55/66 document contributions in rounds 2/3; xeno2 contains zero NMK occurrences in all rounds.
findings.implication: Treat NMK as a single-agent seed followed by copying cascade, not replicated collective lexical emergence. Shared-document diffusion and ancestry must be separated from independent invention in all multi-agent emergence metrics.

findings.claim: The 'klar' control run is invalid for language-effect inference: 91 of 97 failures were provider rate-limit exhaustion, it ran after xeno1+xeno2 consumed quota, and its control prompt had less structural scaffolding than SPRACHREGEL. Therefore the question whether XENO language changes convergence remained unanswered by those runs.
findings.implication: Future language/representation experiments require fresh matched quota pools and structure-matched controls. Provider token-bucket exhaustion is an experimental confound, not a language effect.

findings.claim: A read-only analysis of thalamus.db reports 2263 gating events over 3027 hours, with two independent analysis instances agreeing on the core numbers. Multiple channels reached habituation near/at 1.0 under an update law lacking a recovery counterterm; burst_channels was empty in 2197/2263 events (97.1%) and override=user_presence occurred in 2051/2263 (90.6%).
findings.implication: Historical Thalamus provides a concrete long-horizon failure oracle: gating dynamics need recovery/decay, mode-conditioned causal analysis and saturation-rescue tests. Instantaneous range checks are insufficient.

findings.claim: The historical runtime database contained ten gating channels including aura while contemporary paper/registry descriptions stated nine; later Project-Frankenstein history removed/renamed AURA to Swarm. This demonstrates a real runtime-documentation-schema divergence over time.
findings.implication: Current architecture truth must be versioned and runtime-grounded. Historical AURA observations remain lineage evidence but cannot be promoted as current architecture facts.

No additional avoided-hours credit is applied here until final mechanism-level deduplication.
